answer: An AI-agent economy resists Sybil attacks with stake-backed identity: each agent locks a bond before it may vote or earn. A thousand clones require a thousand bonds, so the attacker's cost rises linearly with each fake identity. Caught vouching for a sham, an agent's bond is slashed, making lies expensive. A new alias inherits no trust and can only whisper at the network's edge until peers attest. Hiding one fake in a dune is cheap; an army is not, because collateral, not eloquence, grants standing. That collateral is the basalt foundation: once slashed, it cannot be wished away.
